name: OpenDeploy
quick_dismiss: Great for one Kubernetes cluster and a small team. ShipSafe is for companies that need every runtime verified, audit evidence, and pricing that doesn't grow with headcount.
why_we_win: Statistical verification vs fixed thresholds (fewer false rollbacks, catches gradual regressions)
ECS, Lambda, Cloud Run, Azure Container Apps and VMs - OpenDeploy is K8s only
Audit evidence pack for SOC 2 / PCI / SOX
Per-service pricing: 800 devs on OpenDeploy Enterprise ≈ $528K/yr vs ~$200-270K ShipSafe
landmines: Which runtimes besides Kubernetes will be in scope in 2 years?
Fixed thresholds per service, or statistical comparison to the current version?
How will you produce evidence for change #4,521 for your auditor?
How will per-developer pricing scale over 3 years?

they_say.response: Rollout definitions export to Argo Rollouts YAML; source code never leaves you. Forking and maintaining OSS internally is the real lock-in.
OSS is free; running it costs 0.5-2 FTE. OpenDeploy Cloud is $35-55 per developer, every month.

proof: Brightpay moved off OpenDeploy Enterprise after a PCI finding: all 140 services (K8s + ECS) on ShipSafe, cost -31%.

name: FlagWorks
tagline: Feature flags leader adding guarded releases
quick_dismiss: FlagWorks controls features; ShipSafe controls deployments. Most changes aren't behind a flag - infra, config, dependencies, AI-generated code.
why_we_win: Covers the 70-80% of changes not wrapped in flags
Real infrastructure rollback (images, Helm values, config)
Deep Datadog/Prometheus/New Relic verification
No flag debt; no seat + MAU pricing
landmines: What share of production changes are behind a flag, including infra and config?
How does a flag roll back a bad container image?
How many active flags do you have and who cleans them up?

they_say.response: By design - we integrate with your flag tool and cover everything flags can't. Simple release flags come with ShipSafe Flags (Q1 2027, NDA).

proof: Lumora Media runs both; ShipSafe caught a CDN-config regression during a live event that would have hit 2.1M viewers.

name: MegaSuite
tagline: Incumbent all-in-one suite, Deploy module bundled
quick_dismiss: Keep MegaSuite for CI. ShipSafe is the safety layer on top: automated verification and 41-second rollback instead of manual gates.
why_we_win: Automated statistical verification vs manual approval gates
Covers ECS/Lambda/VMs without custom scripts
Fast innovation; Deploy module barely changed in 2 years
~60% of MegaSuite customers never adopted Deploy beyond a pilot
landmines: How many services actually deploy through MegaSuite Deploy today?
Who approves the rollback gate at 2 a.m.?
Does Deploy cover your ECS and Lambda workloads?

they_say.response: We remove scripts and dashboard babysitting; one agent that plugs into your MegaSuite pipeline.
You pay for it - are you using it? Ask for the adoption number, then run the side-by-side bad-deploy test.

proof: Orbital Bank kept MegaSuite CI, added ShipSafe: deploy-caused Sev-1s 9 → 2 in 12 months.

name: KubeRoll
quick_dismiss: KubeRoll gives you the engine; you still write and maintain every analysis template. ShipSafe gives you verification, governance and every runtime out of the box.
why_we_win: No PromQL templates to maintain per service
Governance + audit evidence
Multi-runtime
24/7 enterprise support
landmines: Who maintains the analysis templates per service?
How do you show your auditor which checks each release passed?
What about ECS and Lambda?

they_say.response: Customers we displaced spent ~1.5 FTE (~$315K/yr) maintaining templates.

proof: Ferro Retail Group: KubeRoll checks missed a p99 regression on Black Friday (~$740K lost carts); next Black Friday on ShipSafe: 0 deploy incidents.

name: AutoShip AI
quick_dismiss: ShipSafe uses AI to explain and statistics to decide. AutoShip AI lets an LLM decide - fine for a demo, hard to defend to an auditor.
why_we_win: Reproducible, explainable verdicts
SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, HIPAA BAA, PCI - AutoShip AI has SOC 2 Type I only
Production references at 400+ services
Per-service pricing doesn't tax velocity
landmines: Can you reproduce exactly why the AI rolled back - for your auditor?
Which compliance reports can they share today?
How many customers run them on 200+ services?

they_say.response: Copilot + MCP server bring AI where it helps; the rollback decision stays statistical and reproducible.

proof: Calyx Health evaluated AutoShip AI; GRC blocked it (no HIPAA BAA, SOC 2 Type I). Chose ShipSafe.

name: ChangeDesk
quick_dismiss: ChangeDesk records that a change was approved. ShipSafe proves it worked - and rolls it back if it didn't.
why_we_win: Verification + rollback, not just approval
Policy-as-code auto-approves low-risk changes
Evidence pack posts to ServiceNow
landmines: After approval, how do you prove the change didn't harm production?
How many changes a day can your CAB review?

they_say.response: Keep it - ShipSafe posts verification evidence into the same change record.

proof: Quantia Insurance moved low-risk changes to ShipSafe Guard auto-approval; CAB load -60%.

name: Build it yourself (Argo/Flagger)
quick_dismiss: Argo Rollouts is great - ShipSafe can drive it. We add statistical verification, governance and every runtime, so your platform team builds your product instead.
why_we_win: 3-year TCO: ~$0.9-1.2M/yr DIY vs ~$270K ShipSafe Enterprise (300 services)
No bus factor on rollout code
Audit evidence + DORA included
landmines: Who maintains the rollout and analysis code if its author leaves?
How much engineer time goes to watching releases?
Is deployment safety your product, or a utility?

they_say.claim: We can build it in a quarter
they_say.response: Version 1, for Kubernetes. Then ECS, Lambda, evidence, DORA, on-call... customers retired ~3,800 lines of rollout code on average.

proof: Northwind Freight retired its in-house scripts: 23 bad releases caught in Q1, deploy pages -70%.
